name: Nimesulide
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Acute pain; primary dysmenorrhea (adults and adolescents 12 years and older). Second-line only: use only when other NSAIDs or analgesics are not suitable. No longer approved in Europe for osteoarthritis (EMA 2012).
usual_adult_dose.dose: 100 mg twice daily after meals for the shortest time possible; maximum 15 days per course (EMA 2007/2012)

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Other NSAIDs, analgesics; hepatotoxic drugs; alcohol

serious: Serious liver injury, including very rare fatal cases

contraindications: Hepatic impairment; history of nimesulide hepatotoxicity
Active or recurrent ulcer, gastrointestinal or other active bleeding, bleeding disorders
monitoring: Liver injury risk: maximum 15 days per course, second-line only
Hepatotoxicity risk rises with duration over 15 days and higher doses; do not rechallenge after liver injury
Liver tests if any symptoms; stop permanently if abnormal

pk.half_life_eskd: AUC and half-life about 50% higher in mild to moderate impairment, no accumulation
